assumptions: FoldIndex's published formula over normalised Kyte-Doolittle hydropathy and net charge, at the window given.
limits: A 2005 two-term predictor: it sees charge and hydropathy only.
Negative means predicted unfolded, which is not evidence of disorder in the cell.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which stretches of this protein does FoldIndex predict unfolded?

description: Intrinsic disorder along a protein by FoldIndex (Prilusky 2005): I_F = 2.785·⟨H⟩ − |⟨R⟩| − 1.151 over a sliding window, where ⟨H⟩ is mean normalized Kyte-Doolittle hydropathy and ⟨R⟩ the mean net charge per residue. Negative means predicted unfolded. Reports the whole-protein score, the per-window series, the runs below zero, and the Uversky charge-hydropathy point with the boundary it was judged against.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

chargeModel.description: 'net' counts whole charges K+R−D−E, which is what the paper does; 'henderson-hasselbalch' uses fractional charges at `pH`. They answer different questions and only the first is settled by the paper.

countHistidine.description: count histidine as positive in the 'net' model. False by default: the paper says charged residues at pH 7.0, and His (pKa ~6) is ~9% protonated there, so Uversky's set is K,R vs D,E — exposed because some FoldIndex descendants do count it.

pH.description: pH for the Henderson-Hasselbalch model, ignored by 'net' (default 7.0, the pH the paper's ⟨R⟩ is defined at). Only applies when chargeModel is henderson-hasselbalch.

pKaSet.description: named pKa set for the Henderson-Hasselbalch model (default IPC_protein, which is idpr's). Values: EMBOSS (EMBOSS (Rice 2000)), DTASelect (DTASelect (Tabb 2002)), Solomons (Solomons (Solomons 1992)), Sillero (Sillero (Sillero 1989)), Rodwell (Rodwell (Rodwell 1982)), Lehninger (Lehninger (Nelson 2017)), Toseland (Toseland (Toseland 2006)), Thurlkill (Thurlkill (Thurlkill 2006)), Nozaki (Nozaki (Nozaki 1971)), Dawson (Dawson (Dawson 1989)), Bjellqvist (Bjellqvist (Bjellqvist 1994)), ProMoST (ProMoST (Halligan 2004)), IPC_protein (IPC_protein (Kozlowski 2016)), IPC_peptide (IPC_peptide (Kozlowski 2016)), Vollhardt (Vollhardt (Vollhardt 2014)).

protein.description: the protein sequence (unambiguous one-letter codes); wire it from translate_sequence.

window.description: sliding window in residues, odd so a window has a centre residue to report at (default 51, the size the FoldIndex paper uses). Short windows expose single loops; long ones report whole domains.

name: protein_disorder

boundary.description: the Uversky 2000 boundary |⟨R⟩| = 2.785·⟨H⟩ − 1.151 evaluated at this protein's ⟨H⟩ — what `meanNetCharge` is above or below

disorderedFraction.description: that count as a fraction of all windows

disorderedWindows.description: how many windows score below zero

meanHydropathy.description: ⟨H⟩ over the whole chain — the x of the Uversky charge-hydropathy point

meanNetCharge.description: |⟨R⟩| over the whole chain — the y of the Uversky point

overall.description: whole-protein FoldIndex from the global means — the number the 2005 paper's abstract reports. Below zero = predicted unfolded

pKaSetName.description: the pKa set actually used, or '' for the 'net' model which needs none

plot.description: the FoldIndex profile as a plot; below zero is predicted disordered

positions.description: 1-based centre residue of each window, parallel to `scores`

scores.description: just the I_F value per window, parallel to `positions`

segments.description: runs of consecutive negative windows as 1-based inclusive residue spans, with each run's mean and minimum I_F

unfolded.description: whether the whole-protein point sits above that boundary, i.e. predicted natively unfolded

windowCount.description: how many windows were scored — the series length, so a fraction can be read back

windows.description: every window: { position, centerResidue, hydropathy, charge, score } — the series a plot draws
